questions.question: A patient presents with high fever, septic shock, and pancytopenia four days after a dog bite. Which fastidious, gram-negative organism should be suspected, and what are its characteristic clinical presentations?

In the early phase of sepsis, the patient exhibited disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). How does the subsequent development of microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (MAHA) and persistent thrombocytopenia after the resolution of the initial septic phase shift the differential diagnosis?

When evaluating a patient with suspected thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA), how is the measurement of ADAMTS13 activity used to differentiate Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP) from other forms of TMA, such as complement-mediated HUS (CM-HUS)?
Can normal serum C3 and C4 levels rule out a diagnosis of complement-mediated hemolytic uremic syndrome (CM-HUS)? Explain the pathophysiology behind this finding.
What are the hallmark histological findings on a renal biopsy that distinguish thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) from other causes of acute kidney injury, such as isolated acute tubular necrosis?
What is the mechanism of action of eculizumab, and why is it imperative to provide meningococcal vaccination and antimicrobial prophylaxis prior to initiating this therapy?

Contrast the roles of plasma exchange (PEX) and terminal complement inhibitors (e.g., eculizumab) in the treatment of CM-HUS. Why is PEX often viewed as a bridging therapy rather than a definitive cure in this specific condition?
